lines.text: Stormie suddenly touched her and said—‘Is it true that there is an engagement between Mr. Browning and Ba—?’
lines.note: Opens with the moment your secret engagement was nearly exposed at home.

lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: Flush’s frantic welcome shows the home life you two shared.

lines.text: Let them call it ‘felony’ or ‘burglary’—so long as they don’t go to church with us, and propose my health after breakfast!
lines.note: A comic defiance of scandal that frames the elopement as yours alone.

lines.text: Now I will kiss you, dearest: used you to divine that at the very beginning, I have sometimes shortened the visit in order to arrive at the time of taking your hand?
lines.note: A private tenderness about shortening visits to reach her hand.

lines.text: So my reverie was broken in the middle—but being better tempered, rather, than Flush, or having larger resources, I did not growl, but took your latest letter out instead, which lasted for the whole remainder of the time.
lines.note: Shows her turning to your latest letter when the world interrupts her reverie.

lines.text: Shall we do that, when we sit together on the ragged edge of earthquake chasms, in the midst of the ‘sulphurous vapour.’
lines.note: A private image of sitting together on earthquake chasms in sulphurous vapour.

lines.text: And something I said in my letter, which was wrong to say and I am sorry to think of—forgive me that, ever beloved—but you have forgiven, I know.
lines.note: Her direct apology for something said, fitting an occasion of asking forgiveness.

lines.text: The post’s old fault, is it not, this letter that does not come?
lines.note: A shared joke about the post’s old fault in delaying letters.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: The sudden loss of Flush, a vivid turning point in their story.

lines.text: Poor Flush—how sorry I am for you, my Ba!
lines.note: Your immediate sympathy when Flush is taken.

lines.text: Only a few words to tell you that Flush is found, and lying on the sofa, with one paw and both ears hanging over the edge of it.
lines.note: Flush’s return, concrete and comic, after the dog-stealer ordeal.

lines.text: Words can never tell you, however,—form them, transform them anyway,—how perfectly dear you are to me—perfectly dear to my heart and soul.
lines.note: Your declaration that no words can measure how dear she is.

lines.text: Ever dearest, I write a word that you may read it and know how all is safe so far, and that I am not slain downright with the day—oh, such a day!
lines.note: The wedding day itself, with its shock and survival.

lines.text: Your letters to me I take with me, let the ‘ounces’ cry out aloud, ever so.
lines.note: Her refusal to leave your letters behind, even by weight.
